name: Team Voltage
missionStatement: Our mission is to empower students to explore the exciting world of Science, Technology, Engineering, Arts, and Mathematics (STEAM) while fostering a lifelong journey of self-discovery. Through the values of Gracious Professionalism™ and a commitment to teamwork, innovation, and integrity, we aim to inspire and develop the next generation of ethical, enlightened leaders.

values.title: Precision
values.description: We engineer dependable mechanisms and code with a focus on quality, safety, and competitive readiness.

season.summary: We are designing a robust REBUILT robot with faster scoring cycles, higher reliability, and a transparent data pipeline so new students can own the game strategy.
goals: Consistently rank in the top 8 at both regional events
Deploy an adaptive autonomous routine for every alliance partner
Expand season media coverage to unlock two new Einstein-level sponsors

history.title: Scorpsquad Roots
history.description: Team 248 “Scorpsquad” at Satellite High set the foundation for what would become Team Voltage.

history.title: County-Wide Collaboration
history.description: Students from multiple Brevard schools united to solve sponsorship challenges and formed Team Voltage 386.

history.title: Advocates for FIRST
history.description: Voltage presented to the Brevard County School Board, inspiring a district-wide push for FRC and FLL teams.

history.title: Melbourne High Home Base
history.description: The team relocated to Melbourne High School, establishing the build space we still occupy today.

history.title: FLL Host Team
history.description: We began hosting local FIRST LEGO League tournaments, mentoring dozens of younger teams.

history.title: Championship Return
history.description: After major fundraising improvements, Voltage returned to FIRST Championship in Houston.

history.title: Community Programs Expand
history.description: Sparky’s STEAM Camp and year-round outreach events now serve hundreds of students annually.

faqs.question: Who can join Team Voltage?
faqs.answer: Any Brevard County high school student without an FRC team can participate—no experience required.

faqs.question: Do I need prior robotics skills?
faqs.answer: No. We teach CAD, programming, fabrication, business, and media skills with structured onboarding and mentors.

faqs.question: How much does it cost?
faqs.answer: We ask each family to support travel and fundraising, but need-based assistance is available.

faqs.question: How do sponsors help?
faqs.answer: Sponsor funding covers robot parts, event travel, community outreach, and Sparky’s STEAM Camp scholarships.
